correctness.rationale: The exact polynomial vector field is gradient. Its real Hessian is a PSD radial rank-M form minus a rank-two mean-field form. At noncollinear closure the exact tangent-kernel dimension M-2 forces Hessian index (positive M, negative 2, zero M-2), hence Jacobian inertia (2,M,M-2). At collinear closure the Hessian splits into D-c11^T and -c11^T; Sylvester congruence produces the exact threshold R=1. Five exact SymPy eigenvalue computations from the standalone packaged script matched the theorem. Finite tests are not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The complete unstable-mode index, not merely non-attraction or gradient structure, is a sharp all-population stability result across a natural continuum of exact closed-polygon solutions. It identifies the exceptional collinear surface where one radial unstable direction appears and where an additional zero eigenvalue arises. This resolves a motivated stability distinction in a system previously investigated primarily by numerically sampled transverse spectra.
